messages:
elaine: quick sync — proposing a small new stage in the model intake: 'compat-filter' (pre-bench). idea: run cheap ops-only kernel checks + a 100-sample microbench to catch kernel mismatches and noisy perf regressions before models hit full bench. doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/compat-filter :eyes:

ben: +1 on catching this earlier. curious about false positives from noisy infra. how do we avoid flapping?

elaine: good call. proposal includes deterministic seeds, short warmup, and compare to a per-architecture golden baseline. we only block on hard failures (invalid op, serialization error) or >3x median latency regression on the microbench. soft warnings go to telemetry.

sasha: can we reuse runtime's existing "probe" path? we already have a lightweight exec for health checks and small token runs. reuse avoids duplicating kernels.

leo: probe currently lives in eng-runtime and assumes an auth flow + admin-only flags. boundary question: does eng-ml get a stable public shim, or do we add a new minimal gRPC probe endpoint that runtime exposes to pipelines?

elaine: leaning toward a minimal gRPC contract: ExecProbe({model_id, ops_list, seed, max_tokens}) -> {ok|error, p50,p95,errors}. keep it intentionally tiny to avoid coupling.

infra-bot: deployed canary of probe-shim to staging cluster r-compat-02 at 2023-10-31T17:12:45Z. logs available at https://kibana/redwood/compat-shim-canary

ben: what about signal noise from multi-tenant GPUs? do we run jobs on dedicated small instance or use pinned queues?

elaine: plan is to run compat-filter on a "micro-pool" of pinned GPUs (2A) with low co-tenancy. cost tradeoff vs fewer false positives. we can fade to best-effort later when signal trust grows.

maya: metrics question: what thresholds trigger a hard-block? e.g., token-latency p95 >= 3x baseline? flakey op failure rate > 0.1%?

elaine: initial thresholds:
```
# compat-filter thresholds (draft)
latency_block_ratio: 3.0  # p95 > 3x baseline -> hard block
op_error_rate_block: 0.01  # >1% op errors -> hard block
op_failure_block: any invalid-operator / serialization exception -> hard block
samples: 100
seed: 1337
```

sasha: +1 to include a "burn-in" that reruns failing samples 3x before blocking. avoids transient infra flakiness.

leo: also need schema for errors so we can map runtime error -> onboarding UI message. i can sketch a tiny enum: INVALID_OP, KERNEL_MISMATCH, SERIALIZATION_ERR, TIMEOUT, PERF_REGRESSION.

elaine: yep will add that to the contract. also want the compat-filter to emit a compressed trace (KV cache hit pattern + ops sequence) for debug bundles when blocking.

ben: ops_list — do we enumerate a minimal op-set or ask runtime for 'critical_ops' from model metadata? some backbones have fused ops that confuse static lists.

elaine: runtime can expose a per-model op-hint via metadata after initial parse; compat-filter will fetch that and augment with a small canonical op set. fallback to conservative list if missing.

maya: rollout plan? default to warn-only for 2 weeks, then blocking for new models only, and blocking for all after 6 weeks?

elaine: exactly. rollout: warn-only in staging -> warn-only in prod (2w) -> block new-models (4w) -> full block (6w), with metrics gate at each step (false-positive rate < 0.5%).

infra-bot: compatibility diagnostics job created: job-id rcf-compat-2023-11-01, schedule immediate for new intake.

ben: dev experience: need clear failure messages and a one-click bypass for SEV triage. otherwise we'll get noisy tickets.

elaine: agreed — add a "resolve-and-continue" flow in Console that logs an audit entry and tags the model intake with bypass_reason. ephemeral bypass requires a follow-up ticket.

leo: action items I can take: draft gRPC proto for ExecProbe and error enums.

sasha: I'll prototype compat-filter runner that calls probe and emits the microbench.

maya: I'll own the metric dashboards and alert rules (p95 drift, op-error-rate, block-rate).

elaine: thanks team. next sync Friday 11:00 to review proto + sample outputs. short checklist for the doc: 1) proto + error enum, 2) thresholds + rerun policy, 3) micro-pool config, 4) console UX bypass flow, 5) rollout gating metrics.

elaine: (small note) try to keep messages short in the doc link — I added a simple example payload for the ExecProbe in the RFC.
